alexius-meinong.oneLineEn: Theory of objects figure filling language, existence, and non-existent object problems.

alvin-plantinga.oneLineEn: Reformed epistemology and modal ontological argument; fills contemporary philosophy of religion.

andres-bello.oneLineEn: Venezuelan-Chilean thinker who shaped post-independence state-building via law, education, and language.

anibal-quijano.oneLineEn: Peruvian social theorist of the 'coloniality of power' who shaped decolonial theory.

antonio-caso.oneLineEn: Mexican anti-positivist who countered Comtean order with life, ethics, and personhood.

atisa.oneLineEn: Key Kadampa figure whose Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment shaped Tibetan lamrim.
keywordsEn: Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment

aurobindo.oneLineEn: Integral Yoga and evolutionary spirituality linking Vedānta, yoga, and modern Indian thought.

baal-shem-tov.oneLineEn: Hasidic founder whose spiritual joy, piety, and sense of divine presence shaped East European Judaism.

bachelard.oneLineEn: Epistemological rupture and scientific spirit; a source for Foucault's archaeology of knowledge.

badarayana.oneLineEn: Traditional author of the Brahma Sūtras; Vedānta root text shared by the three major commentators.

bahya-ibn-paquda.oneLineEn: Author of Duties of the Heart; joined inner piety and ethical discipline to Jewish legal life.

bhartrhari.oneLineEn: Author of Vākyapadīya; key node of Indian philosophy of language and grammar.

bourdieu.oneLineEn: Habitus, field, and cultural capital; theory of social practice.

boutroux.oneLineEn: Critiqued strict determinism via contingency of natural law; linked French science philosophy and spiritualism.

bruno-latour.oneLineEn: Actor-network theory and anthropology of science; after Canguilhem and Koyré.

brunschvicg.oneLineEn: Philosophy of judgment and history of scientific spirit; hub of French epistemology.

buton.oneLineEn: Tibetan Buddhist historian and key figure in Kangyur/Tengyur redaction.

canguilhem.oneLineEn: The normal and the pathological; history of life sciences; Foucault's direct mentor.
